pages.title: File:Bank of Restriction Flashnote by George Cruickshank (1819).jpg

ObjectName.value: Bank of Restriction Flashnote by George Cruickshank (1819)

Categories.value: George Cruikshank|1819 in the United Kingdom|Counterfeit banknotes|Bank of England Museum|Self-published work|1819 cartoons|Uploaded with Mobile/Android|Capital punishment in the United Kingdom

ImageDescription.value: Cartoon parody of a Bank of England banknote by George Cruikshank in the name of the "Bank of Restriction". The note, decorated with skulls, gallows, and the hangman's noose, protests against the severity of anti-forgery laws in Britain at the time. Forgery remained a capital crime until 1832. Bank of England Museum Collection.

pages.title: File:Bank of England Spitfire Fund Plaque (4 Feb 1941).jpg

ObjectName.value: Bank of England Spitfire Fund Plaque (4 Feb 1941)

Categories.value: Bank of England Museum|Self-published work|Uploaded with Mobile/Android|February 1941 in the United Kingdom|Spitfire Fund

ImageDescription.value: Commemorative plaque commemorating the funds donated to the Spitfire Fund by employees at the Bank of England. A cheque for £5,000 was delivered to the Ministry of Aircraft Production on 4 February 1941. The sum for sufficient for the nominal "purchase" of one Spitfire, dubbed "Old Lady". Collection of the Bank of England Museum.
